en: The Banaue Rice Terraces act as giant inclined planes, reducing the force needed for farmers to carry heavy harvests up the mountain.
Jeepney tires have deep treads to increase friction and prevent sliding on wet Manila roads during the rainy season.
Gravity pulls ripe Guimaras mangoes straight down to the ground once they detach from the branch.
Black sand beaches in Cagayan contain magnetite, a magnetic iron mineral that can be picked up with a strong magnet.
The Tiwi Geothermal Power Plant in Albay converts heat energy from underground volcanic steam into electricity for Filipino homes.
Smooth, polished capiz shells reflect light brightly, making them perfect for decorating traditional Filipino parol lanterns.
The Puerto Princesa Underground River creates a distinct echo when you shout, because sound waves bounce off the limestone walls.
A traditional clay palayok conducts heat slowly and evenly, making it ideal for simmering Filipino sinigang.
Sugarcane in Negros Occidental stores chemical energy that can be converted into bioethanol to fuel vehicles.
The wooden wheels of a carabao-drawn kariton act as wheels and axles to reduce friction when transporting heavy rice sacks.
Hot air rises inside a traditional bamboo bahay kubo, creating convection currents that keep the interior cool.
Rubbing a dried mango leaf against a plastic balloon transfers electrons, creating static electricity to pick up small paper bits.
